name: Sennacherib
bio: Sennacherib, king of Assyria, invaded Judah in Hezekiah's fourteenth year, capturing all its fortified cities. Hezekiah tried to buy him off, stripping the temple and palace of silver and even gold from the temple doors to pay the tribute Sennacherib demanded, but Sennacherib still sent his officers Tartan, Rabsaris, and Rabshakeh with a large army to besiege Jerusalem itself. Rabshakeh, speaking for Sennacherib, mocked Hezekiah's trust in both Egypt and the LORD and warned the people on Jerusalem's wall that no god had ever saved a nation from Assyria's hand (2 Kings 18:13-35). Sennacherib's continued siege and ultimate humiliating defeat are told in detail in the chapters ahead.
